title: Video Streaming (VOD)
summary: On-demand video works by doing the expensive work once and the cheap work millions of times. Each title is encoded ahead of time into a ladder of qualities, cut into short encrypted segments, and spread across a CDN. The player then downloads segments a few seconds ahead, switching quality as the network changes so the picture never stops.

walkthrough.title: Upload the master
walkthrough.text: A studio delivers a mezzanine file: a near-lossless master that can be 100+ GB for a feature film, uploaded in parallel parts to object storage.

walkthrough.title: Encode the ladder
walkthrough.text: The file is split into chunks encoded in parallel into a ladder of renditions, from about 235 kbps at 320p to 15+ Mbps 4K HDR. Per-title encoding picks the ladder that suits each film's complexity.

walkthrough.title: Package and encrypt
walkthrough.text: Renditions are cut into 2 to 6 second CMAF segments, encrypted once, and described by HLS and DASH manifests that work with FairPlay, Widevine, and PlayReady DRM.

walkthrough.title: Start playback
walkthrough.text: The player asks the playback API to play a title. It checks the subscription, region rights, and device, then returns a signed manifest URL and issues a DRM licence.

walkthrough.title: Fetch segments
walkthrough.text: The player downloads segments from the nearest CDN edge. On a miss, the edge fetches from a regional shield and then the origin, but popular titles are pre-positioned overnight.

walkthrough.title: Adapt the bitrate
walkthrough.text: After each segment the player measures throughput and buffer level and picks the next rendition, dropping quality before the buffer runs dry rather than stalling.

walkthrough.title: Report experience
walkthrough.text: The player sends beacons for startup time, rebuffering, bitrate, and errors. Operators use them to pick better CDNs and encodes.

data.label: Content Ingest

input.name: Studio delivery
input.type: Mezzanine: ProRes / JPEG 2000 + audio stems + subtitles

responsibilities: Receives huge masters reliably with resumable, parallel multipart uploads.
Validates the file (checksums, frame rate, audio channel layout) before expensive encoding starts.
Registers metadata, rights windows, and the territories the title may play in.

failureModes.impact: Hours of encoding produce a broken title; audio out of sync.
failureModes.mitigation: Automated QC (checksums, black-frame and audio-sync detection) before encoding.

failureModes.impact: Restarting from zero delays the release.
failureModes.mitigation: Multipart upload resumes from the last completed part.

data.label: Transcoding Pipeline
responsibilities: Encodes chunks in parallel across thousands of machines, then stitches them per rendition.
Picks a per-title ladder: cartoons need far fewer bits than grainy action films.
Scores output quality (VMAF) and re-encodes any rendition that falls below target.

failureModes.impact: Chunks lost; the title is late.
failureModes.mitigation: Chunk-level retries, so only the lost minute is re-encoded.

failureModes.impact: A flicker every minute in the final video.
failureModes.mitigation: Split on keyframe boundaries with closed GOPs and verify with quality checks.

data.label: Packaging & DRM
responsibilities: Cuts every rendition into aligned segments so the player can switch quality at any boundary.
Encrypts once (CMAF with cbcs) so one copy serves Apple, Android, and TV devices.
Registers content keys with the DRM key server; keys never travel with the content.

failureModes.impact: Switching quality causes a visible jump or a decode error.
failureModes.mitigation: Fixed keyframe interval across the whole ladder; validate alignment automatically.

failureModes.impact: Pirated copies of the title spread.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-title (or per-rendition) keys in a hardware-backed key store; rotate keys for live content.

data.label: Origin Storage

input.name: Packaged title
input.type: Segments + manifests (~10-20 GB per title across the ladder)

responsibilities: Holds the master copy of every segment for every title.
Sits behind a shield tier so a CDN cache miss rarely reaches it directly.
Feeds overnight pre-positioning of popular titles to edge caches.

failureModes.scenario: New release: cold caches everywhere at 00:00
failureModes.impact: Millions of misses hit the origin at the same moment.
failureModes.mitigation: Pre-position the title to edges before release; request coalescing at the shield.
Replicate to a second region; most traffic is served from caches anyway.

data.label: Playback & Licence API
responsibilities: Checks subscription, region rights, and concurrent-stream limits before playback.
Chooses a CDN and the formats the device supports (codec, HDR, resolution cap).
Issues DRM licences bound to the device, with output protection rules (e.g. HDCP for 4K).

failureModes.impact: Nothing can start playing, even though the segments are cached everywhere.
failureModes.mitigation: Multi-region licence servers; persistent licences for downloaded content.

failureModes.impact: Freeloaders stream on someone else's account.
failureModes.mitigation: Short expiry, tokens bound to the session, and concurrent-stream enforcement.

data.label: Video Player

output.name: Segment requests
output.type: GET seg_00042.m4s at the chosen rendition

output.name: QoE beacons
output.type: JSON: { startupMs, rebufferMs, bitrate, droppedFrames, errors }

responsibilities: Keeps a buffer (say 30 seconds) and picks each next segment's quality from throughput and buffer level.
Starts fast with a low rendition and climbs, because waiting to start is worse than a soft first few seconds.
Decrypts inside the device's secure hardware path for high-resolution content.

failureModes.scenario: Network drops suddenly (train enters a tunnel)
failureModes.mitigation: Buffer-based ABR switches down early; the lowest rendition is tiny so it almost always loads.

failureModes.impact: The picture keeps sharpening and blurring, which annoys viewers.
failureModes.mitigation: Hysteresis in the ABR logic: switch up slowly, down quickly.

data.label: CDN Edge Caches
responsibilities: Serves segments from servers inside ISPs, close to viewers.
Caches the popular catalogue; popularity follows a power law, so a small share of titles is most traffic.
Validates the signed URL token before serving.

failureModes.scenario: One CDN degrades in a region
failureModes.mitigation: Use QoE telemetry to steer new sessions to another CDN automatically.

failureModes.scenario: Evening peak saturates an ISP link
failureModes.mitigation: Embedded caches inside ISP networks; more efficient codecs (AV1) at peak.

data.label: QoE Telemetry

input.name: Beacons
input.type: Player events every ~10-60 s per session

output.name: Insights
output.type: Rebuffer ratio, startup time by CDN × ISP × device; CDN steering signals

responsibilities: Aggregates playback quality in near real time by CDN, ISP, device, and title.
Feeds CDN steering and alerting when a region's rebuffer rate spikes.
Shows which encodes and ABR tweaks actually improve viewing.

failureModes.mitigation: A lightweight real-time path for key metrics, separate from the full analytics pipeline.

failureModes.impact: The worst sessions are the least visible.
failureModes.mitigation: Send a session-start beacon; treat a missing end beacon as a failure signal.
